# openai_workload_identity_provider (Resource)

Register an OIDC provider for keyless project service-account authentication. Uses the configured OpenAI admin key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openai_workload_identity_provider" "github" {
  name     = "GitHub Actions"
  issuer   = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  audience = "openai"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `audience` (String) Expected audience of workload identity tokens.
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer URL.
- `name` (String) Name of the provider.

### Optional

- `attribute_transformations` (Map of String) Map of attribute names to transformation expressions. Defaults to an empty map.
- `description` (String) Description of the provider.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the provider is enabled. Defaults to true.
- `verification` (Attributes) OIDC verification configuration. Defaults to discovery using the issuer on creation. Omitting this object later preserves the existing configuration; set type = discovery explicitly to restore discovery. Omit discovery_url to use the issuer's discovery endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource ID.

<a id="nestedatt--verification"></a>
### Nested Schema for `verification`

Required:

- `type` (String) Verification method: discovery or uploaded_jwks.

Optional:

- `discovery_url` (String) Custom discovery URL. Only valid for discovery verification.
- `jwks` (String) JSON Web Key Set as a JSON object. Required for uploaded_jwks verification.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import openai_workload_identity_provider.github wip_example
```
